Validating a translation

Source: vignettes/articles/validating-a-translation.Rmd
validating-a-translation.Rmd

A translated model is a claim: this rxode2 model, or this mrgsolve model, is the NONMEM model it came from. This article shows how zupmxio checks that claim, what a comparison report contains, and how a reviewer reads one.

library(zupmxio)

Translate

The example is a two-compartment model with first-order absorption, one of the models that ship with the package. Reading it gives the model as one R object, whatever format it came from:

path <- system.file("corpus", "twocmt-oral", "model.ctl", package = "zupmxio")
model <- pmx_read_nonmem(path)
model
#> <zupmxio_model> read from nonmem
#> Structure: two-compartment closed form, first-order input (ADVAN4 TRANS4)
#> Parameters: 5, initial values only
#> Random effects: ETA1 on CL (exp), ETA2 on V2 (exp)
#> Endpoints: Y (proportional)

Writing it gives the text in the target format and how faithful it is:

mrg <- pmx_write_mrgsolve(model)
pmx_fidelity(mrg)
#> [1] "exact"

A write is one of three things:

  • exact: the written text reads back to the same model.
  • equivalent: a known reparameterisation, such as residual error held as a standard deviation instead of a variance, or NONMEM’s ADVAN4 parameters under rxode2’s linCmt() names.
  • lossy: something was dropped that does not change predictions, such as estimation settings or initial values where the format holds only one value per parameter. pmx_losses() names each item.

A construct that would change predictions is never dropped. The writer stops with an error of class zupmxio_write_error that names it and the formats that can hold it.

Fidelity is a check of the representation: the text reads back as the same model. It does not run the model. That is the comparison’s job.

Compare

pmx_compare() simulates both models and compares their predictions, point by point:

cmp <- pmx_compare(model, mrg)
cmp
#> <zupmxio comparison> pass
#> a: nonmem model, written to rxode2 by zupmxio, on rxode2 5.1.8
#> b: mrgsolve text, simulated as written, on mrgsolve 2.0.1
#> Tolerance: relative 1e-06, absolute 1e-09.
#> 0 of 735 predictions disagree.
#> Worst: ss, subject 15, time 0.5: 4.4041147 against 4.4041147 (abs 6.06e-10, rel 1.38e-10).
#>   regimen points failed  max_abs  max_rel skipped
#>    single    168      0 1.02e-14 8.11e-15        
#>  infusion    168      0 8.44e-15 7.44e-15        
#>  multiple    252      0 1.60e-14 8.68e-15        
#>        ss    147      0 6.06e-10 1.79e-10

Three things decide what a comparison means.

The design. By default, four regimens of 100 units into compartment 1: a single dose, a 2-hour infusion, five doses 12 hours apart, and a dose at steady state. Each is simulated for a typical subject, with every random effect at zero, and 20 subjects whose random effects are drawn from omega with a fixed seed. Residual error is always off: the check is of predictions, not of noise. pmx_design() changes any of this, and gives covariates their values:

pmx_design(n = 5, regimens = c("single", "ss"), covariates = list(WT = 70))
#> <zupmxio design> single, ss, dosing compartment 1
#> The typical subject and 5 with random effects (seed 1).
#> Covariates: WT = 70.

Compartment 1 is NONMEM’s default dose compartment. Into a depot, a single dose is a first-order dose; into a central compartment, a bolus.

The engines. Each side runs on rxode2 or mrgsolve. A written rxode2 or mrgsolve text runs as written, on its own engine: that is the text under test. A model runs on its source format’s engine, and a NONMEM model on rxode2, except that a side never runs on the engine of the other side’s written text. Above, the mrgsolve text runs on mrgsolve, so the NONMEM model runs on rxode2, written by a different writer. A check of the mrgsolve writer that ran both sides through mrgsolve would share its mistakes. engines overrides the choice when there is a reason to.

The tolerance. A point agrees when its relative deviation, abs(a - b) / max(abs(a), abs(b)), is at most tol (1e-6), or its absolute deviation at most atol (1e-9), which covers predictions near zero. A missing or non-finite prediction never agrees. Both engines solve with tight tolerances, so a correct translation agrees far inside tol: the largest relative deviation above is 1.8e-10.

When a comparison fails

Here is a translation with a slip: the central volume is 21 where the source says 20.

slip <- mrg
slip$text <- sub("THETA3 : 20 :", "THETA3 : 21 :", slip$text, fixed = TRUE)
bad <- pmx_compare(model, slip)
bad
#> <zupmxio comparison> FAIL
#> a: nonmem model, written to rxode2 by zupmxio, on rxode2 5.1.8
#> b: mrgsolve text, simulated as written, on mrgsolve 2.0.1
#> Tolerance: relative 1e-06, absolute 1e-09.
#> 735 of 735 predictions disagree.
#> Worst: infusion, subject 5, time 8: 0.26833057 against 0.28530119 (abs 0.017, rel 0.0595).
#>   regimen points failed max_abs max_rel skipped
#>    single    168    168   0.125  0.0592        
#>  infusion    168    168   0.102  0.0595        
#>  multiple    252    252   0.125  0.0587        
#>        ss    147    147   0.119  0.0404

A failed comparison is a value, not an error. bad$predictions holds every point, with both predictions and both deviations, so the pattern of a failure can be read off it. A wrong central volume shows from the first observation on, since every concentration is an amount over it:

p <- bad$predictions
head(p[p$regimen == "single" & p$id == 1, c("time", "a", "b", "rel")], 4)
#>   time        a        b         rel
#> 1  0.5 1.815977 1.736035 0.044021542
#> 2  1.0 2.666641 2.559871 0.040039347
#> 3  2.0 2.968728 2.876659 0.031013093
#> 4  4.0 2.081864 2.061203 0.009924413

Other slips leave other patterns. A wrong lag or bioavailability, for instance, shows only on the regimens and times it touches.

The report

pmx_report() writes a comparison as Markdown, for a reviewer who will not run anything:

file <- tempfile(fileext = ".md")
pmx_report(bad, file, max_points = 3)

It opens with the result, then names the models and how each was simulated:

# Model comparison

**Result: FAIL.** 735 of 735 predictions disagree.

## Models

| Side | Simulated | Engine | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| a | nonmem model, written to rxode2 by zupmxio | rxode2 5.1.8 | nonmem, `model.ctl` |
| b | mrgsolve text, simulated as written | mrgsolve 2.0.1 | written mrgsolve, fidelity exact |

## Design

Regimens single, infusion, multiple, ss, each a dose of 100 into compartment 1.
The typical subject (1) and 20 subjects with random effects drawn with seed 1. Residual error is off.
A point agrees when its relative deviation is at most 1e-06 or its absolute deviation at most 1e-09.

Then the deviations, per regimen, the worst point, and the first points that disagree:

## Results

| Regimen | Points | Disagree | Largest absolute | Largest relative | Skipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| single | 168 | 168 | 0.125 | 0.0592 |  |
| infusion | 168 | 168 | 0.102 | 0.0595 |  |
| multiple | 252 | 252 | 0.125 | 0.0587 |  |
| ss | 147 | 147 | 0.119 | 0.0404 |  |

Worst point: infusion, subject 5, time 8: 0.2683305675 (a) against 0.2853011936 (b), absolute deviation 0.017, relative 0.0595.

### Points that disagree

| Regimen | Subject | Time | a | b | Absolute | Relative |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| single | 1 | 0.5 | 1.815977364 | 1.73603524 | 0.0799 | 0.044 |
| single | 1 | 1 | 2.666641129 | 2.559870558 | 0.107 | 0.04 |
| single | 1 | 2 | 2.968728415 | 2.876658965 | 0.0921 | 0.031 |

And 732 more.

Last come both model texts, exactly as the engines ran them, so the reviewer can see the slip:

## Model b

```cpp
$PROB model.ctl

$PARAM @annotated
THETA1 : 1 : [0, Inf]
THETA2 : 4 : [0, Inf]
THETA3 : 21 : [0, Inf]
THETA4 : 2 : [0, Inf]
THETA5 : 40 : [0, Inf]

$PKMODEL advan = 4, trans = 4, cmt = "DEPOT CENT PERIPH1"

Read a report in this order:

  1. Result. Pass or fail, and how many points disagree.
  2. Models. Which side is the text under test, which engine ran each, and their versions. A side “simulated as written” is the text itself; a side “written by zupmxio” went through another writer.
  3. Design. The regimens, the number of subjects and the seed. The same design and seed give the same random effects, so a comparison can be rerun.
  4. Results. Where the deviations are. A deviation in every regimen points at the structure or a parameter; one regimen alone points at dosing: an infusion, a lag, steady state.
  5. Model texts. What was actually compared.

Against NONMEM output

A NONMEM run’s own tables are the reference closest to the source: they come from NONMEM itself. pmx_read_tables() reads them, and pmx_compare() then simulates the model’s typical subject on the tables’ records and compares it with PRED.

The table here is written the way a NONMEM $TABLE writes one, from the predictions this model is known to make:

expected <- read.csv(system.file(
  "corpus", "twocmt-oral", "expected.csv",
  package = "zupmxio"
))
records <- data.frame(
  ID = 1,
  TIME = c(0, expected$time),
  AMT = c(100, rep(0, nrow(expected))),
  EVID = c(1, rep(0, nrow(expected))),
  PRED = c(0, expected$pred)
)
table <- tempfile(fileext = ".tab")
writeLines(c(
  "TABLE NO.  1",
  paste(sprintf("%-11s", names(records)), collapse = " "),
  apply(records, 1, function(r) paste(sprintf("%11.4E", r), collapse = " "))
), table)
readLines(table, n = 4)
#> [1] "TABLE NO.  1"                                               
#> [2] "ID          TIME        AMT         EVID        PRED       "
#> [3] " 1.0000E+00  0.0000E+00  1.0000E+02  1.0000E+00  0.0000E+00"
#> [4] " 1.0000E+00  5.0000E-01  0.0000E+00  0.0000E+00  1.8160E+00"
tables <- pmx_read_tables(table)
tables
#> <zupmxio tables> 1 subject, 1 dose and 8 observation records
#> Prediction: `PRED`, 5 significant digits.
#> From file1a693c8d5d0b.tab.
pmx_compare(tables, mrg)
#> <zupmxio comparison> pass
#> a: NONMEM table output, column `PRED` (5 significant digits)
#> b: mrgsolve text, simulated as written, on mrgsolve 2.0.1
#> Tolerance: relative 1e-06, absolute 1e-09.
#> 0 of 8 predictions disagree.
#> Worst: table, subject 1, time 6: 1.2738 against 1.2737512 (abs 4.88e-05, rel 3.83e-05).
#>  regimen points failed  max_abs  max_rel skipped
#>    table      8      0 4.88e-05 3.83e-05

NONMEM prints 5 significant digits by default, so no tolerance near 1e-6 could match its tables. The reader records the printed precision, and a point also agrees when the model’s prediction rounds to the table’s value. Covariates come from the table’s columns, and the records may be any design the run had.

What a comparison does not check

  • Residual error. It is off on both sides. The residual model is checked by fidelity, as part of the representation, not by simulation.
  • Individual predictions from a run. Tables are compared on PRED, the typical subject, not IPRED with the run’s random effects.
  • Estimation. Settings such as $ESTIMATION are not translated; reading a control stream records them as lost.
  • Designs it did not simulate. A pass says the models agree on the design they were given. A model with time-varying covariates, or a route the default regimens miss, deserves a design or a table that exercises it.
